text: We were on vacation and my husband really needed an adjustment after our long flight, and he has a chronic knee issue that impacts his back and posture. This was a great experience. The chiropractor was knowledgeable, spoke good English, and had some good suggestions for longterm care and maintenance, too. I speak Thai as well, but he didn’t need any translation. I also appreciated that I asked if I needed an adjustment, and he examined me and said that a little massage would loosen me up so he didn’t need to work on me. He has a conservative approach, and he isn’t in it for the money.

Awesome chiropractor! I went for the first time today. And though it was 1000 Baht for the first trip (500 for subsequent visits) it was worth it. My lower back has been hurting which has been causing my mid and upper back to adjust and hurt as well. The chiropractor spent time talking with me and getting a sense of what’s wrong. His English wasn’t fluent but was very functional. He then popped the mess out of my back! But never in a painful or seeming dangerous way - it was always methodical and smooth. Afterwards, he gave me advice on stretches and exercises to do to help avoid the problem in the future. When I asked if he wanted me to return, I fully expected him to say “oh yeah, this will require many visits” as maximizing income has been a motivation for some of the chiropractors I’ve visited in the past. Instead, he said that I should wait a week and see how I feel. If I still hurt then I should return, otherwise I’m good to go. Very refreshing! Don’t be put off by this being in a neighborhood and at his house. That’s just the way Thais roll sometimes. If you’re looking for a good chiropractor, stop digging cause you’ve struck gold.

text: Krit studied chiropracty in Taiwan. As close as I’ve gotten to a real Palmer chiropractic treatment here in Thailand.

I very rarely leave reviews, but I’ve found one of the best chiropractors ever here in Chiang Mai for a ridiculously cheap price too. I’ve needed regular adjustments for 20 years, which is problematic when travelling and have visited some shockers and charged the Earth for it (£100 for a quack in Jakarta in October). He certainly knows he stuff; identified my subluxations immediately and cleared them with the most gentle manipulations I’ve ever had. As it had been 2 months, there was a lot to do and I went back a week later and was charged only 500. Baht as opposed to 1,000 for a first visit. His place is some 12 kms from town in a suburban street, obviously his home = he’s well cheap; but I’d be prepared to pay way more, he’s that good!

As a chiropractor from the U.S. I knew what my problem was and how best it could be fixed. After trying another Thai chiropractor and many Thai massages I found Chiropractic Chiangmai. The doctor spoke great English, was very knowledgeable about spinal biomechanics and had a nice light touch. I would recommend this chiropractor over many American ones I know.

I had seen many chiropractor throughout my life ( Vietnam, Bangkok, and now Chiangmai) . Of all of them, I think Krit was the best. He was able to fix my neck in just the first visit. Of course I will need to come back for adjustment but I would reccommend him over many licensed American Chiropractor I know. Krit know how to target the problem and fix it right back.

I've been to visit Khun Krit many times now.  He consistently resolves my diversity of odd pains on the first visit. He understands body mechanics, posture and muscle function at a depth I've not seen in most western Chiropractors. He offers precision suggestions for preventing future problems and checks different ways to see that my spine is aligned.  He's practical, down to earth and genuinely caring.

I think Dr. Krit is a genuinely nice guy. However my experience Friday was not a good experience. I called the day before (Thursday) to make an appointment for the following day (Friday 11am). I arrived around 10:45am since it was my first time finding his office. After an unsuccessful attempt to call him. He was nice enough to respond through text to tell me the name of his office (Tiens Massage), which I thought was Chiangmai Chiropractor.

Anyhow, I can understand when unexpected meetings come up. I would understand if he had given me a phone call or text prior to arriving to his office. I don't mind rescheduling because I understand unexpected things arise.  What I don't understand is how a professional like himself didn't honor my appointment time nor give notice or make a simple apology for making a potential client wait forty five minutes. I was very displeased with the level of professionalism. There was no regard for my time.

So let’s start with the positive things. First the chiropractor is very nice and welcoming. He have eased the pain at my back. Also, he gave a lot of advised about the do’s and don’ts on body posture. He also explained certain things on how our body operates and what does it need to operate well. However, he did not addressed all of our concerns. I have an immovable toe but then he just said I just have to massage it. He only addressed my back pain and I thought going to him would be like a holistic treatment in which all of the body alignments will be checked. There were no check ups to other body parts like the shoulders, kneck and whatsoever. Our session only lasted for about 15minutes which is very short and fast for a 1,000 Baht. Aside from that, I also felt a little exaggeration of what he said on the misallignment of my feet. He said the other one is short which he just compressed it well to look shorter. I wish I could show you the picture of what he said as “misalligned feet”. In a nutshell, a thousand Baht for that kind of service is not worth it.

I was VERY hesitant about relying on google reviews to find a chiropractor, but none of the few people I know in Chiang Mai had any referrals.  Alas, I decided to ignore basic common sense and go for it.  (That’s a knock on me, not the chiropractor.)

I called the number listed online and was told I could come immediately.  Great!  So I showered and grabbed a Grab and headed out.  I was about a 20 minute ride away.

For some reason GoogleMap did NOT take me directly to his place.  Instead I was a couple streets off, but luckily my Grab driver agreed to wait for me as I hunted around for the place.  After I tried calling and texting the chiropractor many times for help finding his place, I finally gave up and asked the driver to take me home.  Mai bpen rai, right?  Seriously, I was thinking it AND feeling it:  No big deal; no problem.

Though I was really ready to go home after 15 minutes of walking around in the heat, the driver asked a few neighbors for help finding the place.  Thus, “we” found the chiropractor cleaning in his driveway.  I explained that I’d called and texted, but he apologetically explained that he’d left his phone in the house while he cleaned outside.  Huh?

There was no signage of any kind indicating a chiropractor’s office, and the space in his house is very basic.  Oddly, knowing the driver was waiting for me made me feel a bit more comfortable going forward despite my unease.  It’s just my spine, right?  I mean, what could possibly go wrong, and if it does, I’m only 7,000 miles from home.

My Thai is very bad, so luckily his English is pretty good.  I paid 1000 baht, explained why I needed a chiropractor and he (my apologies, but I’ve totally forgotten his name) motioned me to the table.

I’m a bit of a germaphobe, so when he put the a well-used gel cover over the table hole for my face to rest in, I almost bolted.  Instead, I just sorta tilted my forehead to keep my face off it. That only worked for so long, though, so I tried to zone out the ick factor.

My session lasted 10 or so minutes, and I got my spine cracked, but I’d expected more attention to the specific lower back/hip issue I’d mentioned to him.  I’m no expert though, so maybe he did what needed to be done to address my problem vs having a one-size-fits-all approach to every customer.  Dunno.

At the close he suggested a stretching exercise to help with my lower back/hip issue, and I headed home with my trusty Grab driver.

The chiropractor seems like a really nice guy, but if I had it to do over, I think a traditional Thai massage or two would have been a much wiser use of my baht.

I had such a great experience here! I had some severe back pain with a tingling sensation all over my body and shooting pains down my arms. I booked in immediately and after just ten minutes Dr Krit had realigned me like magic! The pain was gone in an instant. It has now been three days since then and I'm feeling great.

Krit is an excellent professional. He really know chiropractic techniques and how to relief the back pain. I have a lower back protusion, arrive in his place barrelly walking and leave totally with no pain. I've been visiting many chiropracts around the world, and I can assure he's one of the best.

He's a Thai guy who understands and speaks functional english.  I've been to dozen's of chiropractors and had hundreds of adjustments in many countries, and must say he is very good.  Know's his stuff.  Very practical, he even looked at the wear on my shoes and asked many questions to diagnose why my problem is happening.  Gave me specific exercises to loosen the tight muscles creating the problem.

He's in a residential backwater neighborhood in a private residence, but very professional.  First treatment 1,000 baht,  after that 500bt. I would go back.

Relief, kindness and feeling happy again. No longer in pain as the first visit just fixed me right up. This guy is a blessing and has added so much more function to my body and saved me tons of time trying to gradually take it easy and heal on my own. 1000 baht is worth it and I know where to come back to when I need some help at 500 baht for subsequent visits.
